backlog.spec: Replace the binary Morgan bit vector with hashed count vectors: use rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(...).GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy(mol) with the same radius 2 and 2048 bits. Keep the RandomForest unchanged. Counts keep how often each substructure occurs, which matters for lipophilicity since repeated polar groups lower logD.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprint

backlog.spec: Append a small block of physchem descriptors to the fingerprint: Crippen MolLogP, MolMR, TPSA, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3, HeavyAtomCount, and NumAromaticRings, computed with rdkit.Chem.Descriptors / rdMolDescriptors. Concatenate them to the Morgan features before fitting the same RandomForest. Crippen logP is a direct physics-based proxy for the target.
backlog.title: Add Crippen logP and RDKit 2D descriptors

backlog.spec: Compute all ~200 functions in rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.descList for each molecule, replace NaN and inf with 0, and clip extreme values to the 0.1 and 99.9 percentiles of the training set. Concatenate with the Morgan bits and fit the RandomForest. Descriptor-rich features usually beat fingerprints alone on logD.
backlog.title: Full RDKit descriptor set

backlog.spec: Compute the 167-bit MACCS keys with rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys for each molecule and hstack them with the 2048-bit Morgan vector. Keep the RandomForest settings. MACCS encodes coarse pharmacophore presence that complements circular fingerprints.
backlog.title: MACCS keys added to fingerprints

backlog.spec: Swap or add a second fingerprint family using rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator (count fingerprint, 1024 bits) or GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator. Concatenate it with the Morgan features and fit the same RandomForest. Different substructure definitions give the model complementary views of the molecule.
backlog.title: Atom-pair or topological torsion fingerprint

backlog.spec: Use GetMorganGenerator with an atom invariant generator set to FeatureMorganGenerator (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen) at radius 2 with 2048 bits. Feature invariants group atoms into donors, acceptors, aromatic and hydrophobic classes, which generalize better across unseen scaffolds. Keep the RandomForest unchanged.
backlog.title: Feature-based (pharmacophore) Morgan variant

backlog.spec: Change RADIUS from 2 to 3 and N_BITS from 2048 to 4096 to reduce bit collisions and capture larger environments. Keep the RandomForest settings. Larger radius encodes more neighborhood context, though it may overfit scaffold-specific patterns.
backlog.title: Radius sweep for Morgan

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForest with lightgbm.LGBMRegressor using objective='l1' (MAE objective matching the score), n_estimators around 800, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 31, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging_fraction 0.8 with bagging_freq 1, and random_state=seed. Boosting with an L1 objective directly targets the median, which suits the MAE metric.
backlog.title: Gradient-boosted trees (LightGBM) on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Use catboost.CatBoostRegressor with loss_function='MAE', iterations around 1500, learning_rate 0.05, depth 6, verbose=0, random_seed=seed, thread_count=8. Feed the Morgan bit vector. CatBoost's ordered boosting is strong on small tabular data and the MAE loss targets the scored metric.
backlog.title: CatBoost regressor with MAE loss

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto (MinMax-style for count or Jaccard for bit) kernel matrix between molecules from the binary Morgan fingerprints, numpy only: K = (A·B)/(|A|+|B|-A·B). Fit sklearn.svm.SVR with kernel='precomputed', C around 5, epsilon 0.1, and predict on the test-vs-train kernel. Tanimoto kernels are the standard strong baseline for molecular property regression.
backlog.title: Support vector regression with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Build the Tanimoto kernel matrix from binary Morgan fingerprints as in a kernel method, then fit a kernel ridge regressor: solve (K + alpha*I) coef = y_centered with alpha around 0.3, and predict test as K_test @ coef plus the training mean. Use numpy.linalg.solve. This is a fast and well-calibrated smooth model for chemical similarity.
backlog.title: Gaussian process with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Keep the RandomForestRegressor but train it on the target after clipping training y to the 1st and 99th percentiles (winsorize). Outlier measurements in logD distort squared-error splits; clipping reduces their pull on leaf means. Predict on unclipped test features.
backlog.title: Random forest with MAE criterion-like median leaves

backlog.spec: Keep the model, but fit on standardized target: y_s = (y - mean)/std of train_y, and invert the transform on predictions. For a RandomForest the scale does not change splits, so instead try a robust scaling with median and IQR as a sanity variant. Keep it only if it changes predictions; otherwise it is a no-op and should be dropped.
backlog.title: Log-transform or standardize target

backlog.spec: Fit both the RandomForest (existing settings) and an LGBMRegressor with objective 'l1' on the same Morgan features, then average their test predictions with equal weights. Model diversity between a bagged forest and a boosted model typically lowers error more than tuning either one alone.
backlog.title: Ensemble of RF and LightGBM

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, make an out-of-fold 5-fold split of the training data, collect predictions from RandomForest, LightGBM (objective l1) and SVR-Tanimoto (or kNN), then fit a non-negative linear regression (sklearn LinearRegression positive=True) on the OOF predictions to get blend weights. Refit base models on all training data and apply the weights to test predictions.
backlog.title: Stacking with ridge meta-learner

backlog.spec: Set MAX_FEATURES to 0.5 (or sqrt), MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF to 2, and N_TREES to 500. Leaf size and feature fraction control variance on noisy experimental targets. Keep the rest of the pipeline identical.
backlog.title: Deeper tuning of RandomForest hyperparameters

backlog.spec: After the RandomForest fits, compute residuals on the training set using out-of-bag predictions (oob_prediction_ with bootstrap=True, oob_score not needed). For each test molecule, find its 5 nearest training neighbours by Tanimoto similarity and add the mean of their OOB residuals, weighted by similarity, to the RF prediction. This pushes local chemical-series trends into the output.
backlog.title: k-nearest-neighbor residual correction

backlog.spec: Train the RandomForest with three different random_state values derived from seed (seed, seed+1, seed+2), each with N_TREES=300, and average predictions. Averaging independently seeded forests reduces variance from the random feature subsampling, at a higher compute cost that still fits within the 10-minute job limit.
backlog.title: Multi-seed bagging of tree models

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesRegressor using n_estimators=500, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, n_jobs=-1, random_state=seed. Extremely randomized split thresholds smooth predictions and often generalize better when test skeletons differ from training ones.
backlog.title: Extra-Trees regressor

backlog.spec: Compute the Bemis-Murcko scaffold (MurckoScaffold.GetScaffoldForMol) and the generic scaffold for each molecule. Add the Morgan fingerprint of the scaffold itself as extra bits, plus the number of ring systems and scaffold atoms. Because evaluation uses unseen scaffolds, scaffold-level descriptors give the model explicit information about ring-core lipophilicity.
backlog.title: Scaffold-aware group feature

backlog.spec: Count ionizable groups with SMARTS patterns: carboxylic acids '[CX3](=O)[OX2H1,OX1-]', aliphatic amines '[NX3;H2,H1,H0;!$(NC=O);!$(N-a);!$(N-S(=O))]', amidines, and tetrazoles. Add these counts and a simple ionization flag as features beside the fingerprint. logD depends strongly on pH-dependent ionization, which Morgan bits capture only indirectly.
backlog.title: Ionizable-group features

backlog.spec: Train a sklearn HistGradientBoostingRegressor with loss='absolute_error' on the same features (Morgan plus RDKit descriptors), using max_iter 600, learning_rate 0.05, max_leaf_nodes 31, l2_regularization 1.0, and random_state=seed. The absolute error loss makes predictions robust to measurement outliers.
backlog.title: Huber-style robust regression head

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, do a small random search (about 8 configurations) over RandomForest max_features in {0.1, 0.3, 0.5} and min_samples_leaf in {1, 2, 4}, scored by 3-fold KFold inner MAE on the training data only (no test data used). Refit the best configuration on all training data. Selection uses only training folds, so it is a valid tuning step inside the harness.
backlog.title: Hyperparameter search with inner CV

backlog.spec: Set RandomForest bootstrap=True with max_samples=0.7 to train each tree on a 70% subsample of molecules instead of the full bootstrap. Smaller per-tree samples add row-level regularization and decorrelate trees, which can reduce overfitting to specific training series.
backlog.title: Dropout-style feature subsampling via bootstrap

backlog.spec: Instead of the mean of tree predictions, return the median of the per-tree predictions for each test molecule (stack model.estimators_ predictions on test features and take np.median along the tree axis). MAE is minimized by the conditional median, so this aligns the point estimate with the scoring metric.
backlog.title: Quantile-median prediction from forest leaves

backlog.spec: Reduce the 2048-bit Morgan vector to the columns that are set in at least 2 training molecules (drop rare and constant bits) before fitting. This removes sparse noise features that dilute random feature sampling in tree models, while keeping the fingerprint length meaningful for the model.
backlog.title: Kernel PCA-free dimension reduction

backlog.spec: Train two separate RandomForests: one on the RDKit physchem descriptors only, one on the Morgan bits only. Average their predictions with weights 0.5 each. Separate models avoid the descriptor features being drowned out by the many fingerprint bits when max_features is sampled.
backlog.title: Mixture of descriptor-only and fingerprint-only models

backlog.spec: Add a feature that is the training-set mean target of the nearest molecular-weight bin, computed in fit_predict on training data only (use 10 quantile bins on MolWt). For test molecules, use the bin mean learned from training. It gives the tree an explicit, smoothed prior for size-dependent lipophilicity trends.
backlog.title: Target-encoding by molecular weight bins

backlog.spec: Build a character n-gram (n=2 to 4) bag-of-counts vector from the canonical SMILES strings, fitting a sklearn CountVectorizer(analyzer='char', ngram_range=(2,4), max_features=1024) on the training SMILES only. Concatenate with the Morgan features and fit the RandomForest. Text-like encodings add complementary, non-graph information about atom and bond patterns.
backlog.title: Pretrained-free SMILES character n-gram features

backlog.spec: Weight each training molecule in the RandomForest fit with sample_weight equal to the inverse of the kernel density estimate of train_y (scipy.stats.gaussian_kde, evaluated at each target value, normalized to mean 1). Down-weighting the dense central region of logD lets the forest devote capacity to the tails, which MAE penalizes equally.
backlog.title: Sample weighting by target density

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, keep loss_function='MAE' but change the CatBoostRegressor call to add leaf_estimation_method='Newton' and leaf_estimation_iterations=10. Leave the featurizer, ITERATIONS, LEARNING_RATE and DEPTH unchanged. This changes only how leaf values are optimized (second-order steps on the MAE gradient instead of the default), so the change is a single argument pair in the model constructor. Watch the 10-minute job limit, since Newton steps can slow fitting slightly.
backlog.title: Newton leaf estimation under MAE loss

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, split train into 90% sub-train and 10% validation with a seed-derived shuffle. Fit CatBoost (loss MAE, LEARNING_RATE=0.02, DEPTH=6, up to 4000 iterations) with eval_set=validation and use_best_model=True, and record best_iteration_. Then refit a fresh CatBoost on all training data with iterations = int(1.1 * best_iteration_) and the same settings, and predict the test set. Use the seed for both the split and the model. This is a schedule change: a lower learning rate with the iteration count chosen by early stopping instead of a fixed 1500.
backlog.title: Inner-holdout early stopping, then refit with a lower learning rate

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold (MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles) for each training molecule. Using numpy RandomState(seed), draw 5 bootstrap-like subsamples, each formed by sampling 85% of the unique scaffolds without replacement and keeping all molecules with those scaffolds. Train one CatBoostRegressor (loss MAE, the existing settings, a different random_seed per bag derived from seed) on each subsample, and return the mean of the 5 test predictions. Scaffold-level subsampling makes each bag see a different chemotype mix, which is a different kind of diversity from seed-only bagging. Keep total time under the 10-minute limit by using ITERATIONS=1000 per bag if needed.
backlog.title: Scaffold-group bootstrap bagging of CatBoost

backlog.spec: Compute heavy-atom count for every train and test molecule. Choose the threshold as the median heavy-atom count of the training set. Train two CatBoostRegressor models (loss MAE, existing settings, random_seed=seed), one on molecules at or below the threshold and one on those above. For each test molecule, predict with the model for its size bin. Fall back to a single model trained on all data for a bin with fewer than 50 training molecules. This routes small and large molecules to specialized trees, which differs from the descriptor-vs-fingerprint split already tried.
backlog.title: Size-split mixture of experts

backlog.spec: Add a per-molecule 3D descriptor block to featurize. For each molecule, add hydrogens, embed one conformer with rdDistGeom.ETKDGv3 using randomSeed=0 (fixed for reproducibility), optionally MMFF-optimize it, then compute rdMolDescriptors.CalcPBF, CalcPMI1, CalcPMI2, CalcPMI3, CalcNPR1, CalcNPR2, CalcRadiusOfGyration, and CalcAsphericity. Use 0 for molecules where embedding fails. Cache results in a module-level dict keyed by canonical SMILES so repeated featurization across the 15 fits is cheap. Append these 8 values to the existing feature vector. Shape-related properties may affect partitioning and membrane partitioning behaviour that fingerprints do not capture.
backlog.title: Cached 3D shape descriptors from one ETKDG conformer

backlog.spec: Add a small block of extra features to featurize. For each molecule, count atoms of each element C, N, O, S, F, Cl, Br, I, P, and count total halogens, formal charges (positive and negative separately), aromatic nitrogens, and hydrogen-bond-free heteroatoms. Compute Gasteiger partial charges (rdPartialCharges.ComputeGasteigerCharges) and append the minimum, maximum and sum of absolute charges, and the number of atoms with |charge| > 0.3. Append these to the existing Morgan plus descriptor vector. The element and charge counts give direct signals for lipophilicity effects of halogens and polar groups that the Morgan bits only capture indirectly.
backlog.title: Elemental composition and charge-distribution features

backlog.spec: Keep the featurizer and the model family, but change the CatBoostRegressor constructor to add rsm=0.5 (feature subsampling per split), l2_leaf_reg=10, random_strength=2, and bootstrap_type='Bernoulli' with subsample=0.7. Keep loss_function='MAE', LEARNING_RATE=0.05, DEPTH=6 and ITERATIONS=1500. The aim is to reduce overfitting to training skeletons, since test folds contain unseen scaffolds, and the random feature and row subsampling should help generalization. These are all constructor arguments, so the edit is small.
backlog.title: Stronger CatBoost regularization for scaffold generalization

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, before fitting, compute the 1st and 99th percentiles of train_y. Drop training rows whose label falls outside this interval, using only those rows for CatBoost fitting (features and labels in the same index mask). Keep the test prediction and all other settings unchanged. Measured logD data often contains noisy or assay-outlier values, and MAE is still sensitive to the placement of the tree leaves that absorb them. Trimming is a one-line mask on X_train and y_train.
backlog.title: Training-label outlier trimming

backlog.spec: Transductive variant inside fit_predict. Fit the existing CatBoost model on the training data and predict the test molecules. Select the 30% of test molecules whose predictions fall closest to the training label median... instead use the 30% whose predictions have the smallest nearest-neighbour Tanimoto distance to the training set (compute with DataStructs.BulkTanimotoSimilarity on the Morgan bit vectors, taking the max similarity). Append those test features with their predicted labels to the training set and refit a fresh CatBoostRegressor with the same settings and seed. Return the refit's predictions for the test set. This uses unlabelled test structure, which the harness allows since fit_predict receives the test SMILES.
backlog.title: Self-training with confident test pseudo-labels

backlog.spec: Replace the single model in fit_predict with an average of three CatBoostRegressor models trained on the same features with loss MAE, LEARNING_RATE=0.05, ITERATIONS=1500, random_seed=seed, and DEPTH in {4, 6, 8}. Average their test predictions with equal weights. Depth variation gives models with different interaction orders, which is a different kind of diversity from seeds, and it adds only a short loop. Check that the total fitting time of all 15 folds stays under 10 minutes, and drop depth 8 if it does not.
backlog.title: Quantile-averaged CatBoost ensemble across depths

backlog.spec: Before training, fit a one-variable linear regression of train_y on Descriptors.MolLogP (Crippen) over the training molecules, using least squares. Subtract that baseline to get residuals, and train the existing CatBoost MAE model on the residuals. At prediction time, add the same baseline back to the test predictions, using the test molecules' MolLogP. Keep everything else (features, ITERATIONS, DEPTH) unchanged. The idea is that the tree model only has to learn what logP misses, which may be easier for a shallow tree ensemble to extrapolate across scaffolds.
backlog.title: Residualize the target on Crippen logP

backlog.spec: Augment the training set by enumerating K=5 randomized (non-canonical) SMILES per training molecule with Chem.MolToSmiles(mol, doRandom=True, canonical=False), seeded from the seed argument via Chem.SetDefaultRandomSeed or by reseeding. Labels are copied to each variant. Build Morgan+descriptor features for every variant and fit one CatBoost model on the stacked set. For test molecules, predict on K randomized SMILES variants and average the predictions. Hold the ITERATIONS fixed, but if training time approaches the 10 minute budget, reduce K to 3.
backlog.title: Randomized-SMILES augmentation with test-time averaging

backlog.spec: Train the existing CatBoost MAE model once with ITERATIONS=1500. Instead of using only the final model, call model.staged_predict(X_test) (or the equivalent with ntree_end) and collect predictions at iterations 600, 900, 1200, and 1500. Average the predictions from the last three checkpoints, so the ensemble uses a smoothed version of the boosting path. This adds no extra training cost. Choose the checkpoints from the seed-independent schedule above, not from the test folds.
backlog.title: Snapshot averaging over CatBoost iteration checkpoints

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, after featurizing the training set, compute the absolute Spearman correlation between each of the 2048 Morgan bits and train_y, using only the training fold. Keep the 400 bits with the highest correlation, plus all 9 physchem descriptors and the Crippen logP feature. Apply the same column selection to the test features. Train the existing CatBoost MAE model on the reduced matrix. The selection must happen inside fit_predict so it never sees test labels. This differs from earlier rare-bit filtering because it uses the label.
backlog.title: Within-fold supervised bit selection

backlog.spec: Build a small fully connected network in numpy: quantile-transform (or standardize) the Morgan bits and descriptors, then use two hidden layers of 256 and 64 units with ReLU, dropout of 0.2 during training, and a single linear output. Train with an L1 (MAE) loss using Adam (lr 1e-3, weight decay 1e-4), batch size 64, for about 150 epochs, with a fixed seed derived from the seed argument. Train 5 such networks with different sub-seeds and average their predictions. Add a time guard so the whole fit stays under 60 seconds per fold. Finally, blend the MLP predictions with the CatBoost predictions at 0.3/0.7 weights.
backlog.title: L1-loss MLP ensemble in numpy

backlog.spec: Within fit_predict, for each training molecule compute the Tanimoto similarity (Morgan bit vectors) to every other training molecule. Use an inner 5-fold split so that each training row's kNN feature is computed only from the other inner folds' labels. The feature is the similarity-weighted mean label of its k=10 nearest neighbours, along with the top-1 similarity. For test molecules, compute the same feature using all training molecules. Append these two columns to the existing features and train the CatBoost MAE model. The out-of-fold construction keeps the feature from leaking a row's own label into its training representation.
backlog.title: Stacked kNN-label feature with inner out-of-fold encoding

backlog.spec: Within fit_predict, split the training set into 4 inner folds. Train the CatBoost MAE model on three inner folds and predict the held-out fold, repeating for all four, to get out-of-fold predictions for every training row. Fit an isotonic regression (sklearn IsotonicRegression, out_of_bounds='clip') mapping out-of-fold predictions to true labels, using an absolute-error-like objective approximated by fitting on the median-binned values. Then train the final CatBoost model on all training data and pass its test predictions through the isotonic map. The goal is to correct systematic shrinkage toward the mean that tree models show at the extremes of logD.
backlog.title: Post-hoc isotonic recalibration on inner out-of-fold predictions

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan fingerprint with a Weisfeiler-Lehman style count vector. For each molecule, initialize each atom's label with a tuple of atomic number, degree, formal charge, and aromaticity. Run 3 refinement iterations, where each atom's new label is a hash of its own label plus the sorted labels of its neighbours. Count how many times each label occurs across all iterations. Build the vocabulary from the training fold only, keep the 2048 most frequent labels, and set unseen test labels to zero. Concatenate the resulting counts with the existing physchem descriptors and train the CatBoost MAE model. This gives a substructure representation that is not tied to RDKit's bit hashing.
backlog.title: Weisfeiler-Lehman subtree count features

backlog.spec: Change the CatBoost configuration only. Set bootstrap_type='Bayesian' with bagging_temperature=1.0, which gives each tree a random sample weight, and set random_strength=2.0 so that split scores are perturbed. Keep depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, and ITERATIONS=1500. Within fit_predict, run this configuration on a 90/10 split of the training fold to choose between bagging_temperature values of 0.5, 1.0, and 3.0 by validation MAE, then refit on the full training fold with the chosen value. Use the seed argument for every random choice. This is a different knob set from plain feature subsampling and L2 regularization.
backlog.title: Bayesian bootstrap and random-strength regularization sweep

backlog.spec: Fit a second base model: a HuberRegressor (sklearn, epsilon=1.35) on the standardized physchem descriptors alone, which is a linear, robust model. Fit the existing CatBoost MAE model on the full feature set. Average the two sets of test predictions with weights 0.8 for CatBoost and 0.2 for the linear model. Choose the blend weight once from a fixed set {0.0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3} using a 10% inner holdout of the training fold, and keep it fixed. The linear model provides a smooth extrapolation component that tree models cannot produce outside the training range.
backlog.title: Blend CatBoost with a robust linear model on descriptors

incumbent.description: Replace RandomForestRegressor with CatBoostRegressor using MAE loss for better performance on small tabular datasets.

memo:
Helped: physchem features (Crippen logP plus RDKit 2D descriptors) added to Morgan bits were the biggest gain, 0.6030 (-0.1200). Swapping RF for CatBoost with MAE loss gave the incumbent, 0.5718 (-0.0184). The kNN residual fix reached 0.5902 (-0.0127) but still needs an ablation.

Did not help: rare-bit filtering (0.7231), Tanimoto SVR (0.6491), ExtraTrees (0.6140), count Morgan (0.5930), Atom Pair bits (0.5862), full descList (0.7202), stacking (2.2158), 3D shape descriptors (0.5718, +0.0000), stronger regularization (0.5756). Small gains within noise sd 0.0042: 3-seed bagging (0.5668/0.5689), depth ensemble (0.5682), radius 3 with 4096 bits (0.5671/0.5703), and inner-holdout early stopping (0.5640/0.5643, -0.0076). Early stopping is the best lead.

Waste: 5 crashes and 4 patch failures early on. Copy SEARCH text exactly.

Next: combine the small gains (early stopping, bagging, radius 3), then try MACCS keys and a CatBoost+LightGBM blend. Replicate any combined result. Watch the 10 min limit.
